findings.text: The two equality assertions compare ask_path's and presentation_path's names against calls to readably_named with the same identity, and both sides resolve through that one rule, so they hold whatever the rule says (the previous copy at lead_presentation.py:325 produced exactly this string for this 26-character identity). Only the hasattr check at line 87 distinguishes the copy, and a copy taking `from hashlib import sha256` or importing hash the local way would pass it, so the naming rule's single-owner claim rests on a structural check rather than on behaviour.

readably_named is a third variant of the readable-stem-plus-digest naming rule the repository already owns: reckon/crew/obligation_snapshot.py:245 `_lock_stem` pairs `_token` with 12 hex digits and reckon/ledger.py:3272 builds the same shape trimmed to 48 characters. The new public helper neither extends nor wraps either owner, so the rule now has three implementations that must be kept in step; the commit fixed the two copies inside the answer store but did not search outside it.

The record's "The same tests pass at the head" block quotes the pre-repair run — revision 81b39dc9bb, 10 passed — while the head it is committed at is d09ba36a with 13 passed in measure/head-tests.log, so a reader of the plan-linked record sees a gate that predates the five repairs and does not show them holding together.
